Cyber-physical systems (CPSs) are complex engineered systems that integrate a cyber layer with physical systems.
Decentralized data injection attacks (DIAs) are a type of attack that compromises the data integrity of CPSs.
The attacker's goal is to corrupt the measurements by injecting a random attack vector to compromise the data integrity while guaranteeing a low probability of attack detection.
The cost function ϕ : Rm→R is used by the attacker to determine the optimal attack vector.
The random attack vector Am follows a multivariate Gaussian distribution with zero mean and variance v.
The covariance matrix of the random attack vector Am is Σ AA= v ie ieT i.
The observation model for state estimation corrupted by noise is Ym=Hx+Zm.
The vector of compromised measurements Ym follows a multivariate Gaussian distribution P Y Am=N(0,Σ YAYA).
The Nash Equilibrium is a state in which no player can improve their payoff by unilaterally changing their strategy.
The potential function is a function that captures the strategic interaction between players and is used to determine the Nash Equilibrium.
The decentralized attack construction is formulated as a potential game.
The best response dynamics is used to achieve the Nash Equilibrium of the game.
The game theoretic approach is used to model and quantify the security of CPSs.
The maximum entropy distribution is used to assign a distribution to the state variables.
The Gaussian assumption is used to model the random attack vector Am.
The multivariate Gaussian distribution is used to model the vector of compromised measurements Ym.
The Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence is used to measure the disruption of the attack.
The mutual information is used to measure the information loss induced by the attack.
